meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and did anyone speak to him before they did?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now, did you speak to Owen before you entered it, and what do you have?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Turn the screen. I'll read the dates myself. And "no drafts before that" proves what, exactly, Hale?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
Hand me the text. I'm searching it myself, and I'm writing down the page you give me. A wrong quotation in an essay is a mistake, Hale, and it doesn't prove anything.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

I know what 4.4 says, I printed it. The zero comes off the gradebook today, and I want in writing, from you and the principal, that nothing goes on his file. Then we talk about Thursday: who else is in that room?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook today, written confirmation from you and the principal that nothing goes on Owen's file, and the name of everyone who would be in the room on Thursday. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback; she agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook today, a written promise that nothing goes on his file, and to know who would be in the room for a rewrite.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times and a quoted line she could search herself, because she could check both without taking your word.
What cost ground: Offering the rewrite while the zero still stood, because it let her demand the zero come off first and the no-record promise in writing.
Try next time: When you offer the Thursday rewrite, say in the same sentence that the zero comes off the gradebook today and that you will email the no-record promise that evening.
